newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FX FUTURES TRADERS WARY OF SURGING DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FX FUTURES TRADERS WARY OF SURGING DOLLAR.

text.p: The dollar's surge on international spot markets continued to inhibit Hungary's currency futures traders on Monday, with most of the modest turnover taken up by December dollar/mark basket deals.

Basket deals, by which dollars and marks are traded in the 30/70 proportion they represent in the central bank's currency basket against which the forint floats, are seen as a way of hedging against large dollar/mark fluctuations.

On the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), which saw turnover worth 1.89 billion forints, the December dollar broke the 200-forint barrier, rising 3.15 to 202.45, while the December mark fell 0.59 to 140.11.
The largest fall in the mark was for next June, which dropped 1.20 to 121.00 forints.

The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) saw just 82 million forints' worth of turnover, taken up by mark deals for this July, which fell 2.00 forints to 107.48 and December, which fell 0.55 to 114.20. The untraded March 1998 mark also fell, by 0.85 to 117.90.

The dollar rose on the BSE by 1.61 forints for August, 2.50 for September and 2.05 for December to 193.95, 195.45 and 201.50 respectively, leaving the December 1997 maturity almost a full forint cheaper than on the BCE.
